t.3.13.1: Then, while going to Pañcavaṭī, Raghunandana met on the way a vulture of huge body and terrible prowess.
t.3.13.2: Seeing him there in the forest, the two illustrious ones, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, took the bird to be a rākṣasa and asked, "Who are you?"
t.3.13.4: Understanding him to be his father's friend, Rāghava honored him, and then he calmly asked him about his lineage and his name.
t.3.13.3: With a sweet and gentle voice, as if to delight the two of them, he said: "Dear child, know me to be a friend of your own father."
t.3.13.5: Hearing Rāma's words, the bird told him of his lineage and of himself, and of the origin of all beings.
t.3.13.6: O mighty-armed Rāghava, hear from me as I recount them all from the beginning, those who were the Prajāpatis in former times.
t.3.13.7: Kardama was the first of them, and Vikṛta came after him; then Śeṣa, and Saṃśraya too, and the mighty Bahuputra.
t.3.13.8: Sthāṇu, Marīci and Atri, and the mighty Kratu, Pulastya and Aṅgiras too, Pracetas, and likewise Pulaha.
t.3.13.9: Dakṣa, Vivasvān, and another, Ariṣṭanemi, O Rāghava; and the mighty, splendid Kaśyapa was the last of them.
t.3.13.10: O Rāma of great renown, we have heard that the Prajāpati Dakṣa had sixty illustrious daughters.
t.3.13.11: Of them, Kaśyapa took eight slender-waisted maidens as his wives: Aditi and Diti, Danu and also Kālakā.
t.3.13.12: Tāmrā and Krodhavaśā, and Manu and Analā as well. Then Kaśyapa, pleased, spoke again to those maidens.
t.3.13.13: "You shall indeed bear sons equal to me, lords of the three worlds." Aditi set her mind on this, O Rāma, and so did Diti and Danu.
t.3.13.14: And Kālakā too consented, O mighty-armed one, but the rest were unwilling. Of Aditi were born the thirty-three gods, O subduer of foes.
t.3.13.15: These are the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras and the two Aśvins, O scorcher of foes. Diti, however, my dear, gave birth to illustrious sons, the Daityas.
t.3.13.16: Formerly this earth, with its forests and oceans, belonged to them. Danu, however, gave birth to a son, Aśvagrīva, O subduer of enemies.
t.3.13.18: Tāmrā too gave birth to these five daughters, renowned throughout the worlds. Krauñcī brought forth the owls, and Bhāsī gave birth to the bhāsa birds.
t.3.13.19: Śyenī gave birth to hawks and vultures of great splendour, while Dhṛtarāṣṭrī bore swans and kalahaṃsa geese of every kind.
t.3.13.17: Kālakā too gave birth to Naraka and to Kālaka, and likewise to Krauñcī, Bhāsī and Śyenī, to Dhṛtarāṣṭrī and also to Śukī.
t.3.13.20: And that lovely lady, too, gave birth to the cakravākas, may good fortune be yours; Śukī gave birth to Natā, and Vinatā was the daughter of Natā.
t.3.13.21: O Rāma, Krodhavaśā too gave birth to ten daughters born of herself: Mṛgī and Mṛgamandā, and Harī and Bhadramadā as well.
t.3.13.22: She bore Mātaṃgī, then Śārdūlī, Śvetā and likewise Surabhi, Surasā, endowed with every auspicious mark, and Kadrukā as well.
t.3.13.23: All the deer are the offspring of Mṛgī, O best among the foremost of men, and from Mṛgamandā sprang the bears, the sṛmaras, and likewise the camaras.
t.3.13.24: Then Bhadramadā gave birth to a daughter named Irāvatī, and her son is Airāvata, the great elephant, protector of the world.
t.3.13.25: The offspring of Harī are the lions and the monkeys who dwell as ascetics; and Śārdūlī gave birth to sons, the golāṅgūla monkeys and the tigers.
t.3.13.26: The elephants are the offspring of Mātaṃgī, O bull among men, and Śvetā gave birth to a son, the white-eyed elephant of the quarters.
t.3.13.27: Then, O Rāma, the goddess Surabhi gave birth to two daughters, Rohiṇī by name, good fortune be with you, and the illustrious Gandharvī.
t.3.13.28: Rohiṇī gave birth to cows, and Gandharvī bore horses as her sons; Surasā brought forth the Nāgas, O Rāma, and Kadrū the serpents.
t.3.13.30: From the mouth the brāhmaṇas were born, and likewise the kṣatriyas from the chest; from the thighs the vaiśyas were born, and from the feet the śūdras. Thus says the śruti.
t.3.13.29: Manu, wife of the great-souled Kaśyapa, gave birth to human beings: brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas and śūdras, O bull among men.
t.3.13.32: Kadrū gave birth to the thousand-headed Nāga who supports the earth, while Vinatā had two sons, Garuḍa and Aruṇa.
t.3.13.31: Analā too gave birth to all the trees that bear auspicious fruits. Vinatā was the granddaughter of Śukī, and Kadrū was the sister of Surasā.
t.3.13.33: From that Aruṇa I was born, and Sampāti is my elder brother. Know me as Jaṭāyu, the son of Śyenī, O subduer of foes.
t.3.13.35: Rāghava, having honored Jaṭāyus in return and joyfully embraced him, bowed down before him; for the self-possessed one had heard from Jaṭāyus, again and again, the account of his friendship with his father.
t.3.13.34: So I shall be your companion in your dwelling here, if you wish, and, dear son, I shall guard Sītā whenever you have gone out together with Lakṣmaṇa.
t.3.13.36: Having entrusted Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, there to that exceedingly mighty bird, he went together with him and with Lakṣmaṇa to that Pañcavaṭī, eager to burn up his enemies as fire burns moths.
